request.task: T3D closure for AI teammate Canvas architecture, threat model, and authority digest
request.head: 899b39433c4be242b4b3adcd39f3e6cd53df99c0

findings.scenario: A syntactically valid dash- or underscore-leading path id (T3A example `-abc1`) is accepted. Architecture says that path ID is validated and echoed into the job. The corrected route leaves response runId as the parsed path id but writes job.projectId as a verbatim copy only for alphanumeric-leading ids; dash/underscore-leading ids are prefix+hex-mapped, and jobId omits run/project identity. Docs claim identity-preserving echo that the bounded route does not perform.
findings.remediation: Replace “echoed into the job” with the T3A rule: HTTP runId stays the parsed path id; job.projectId is a byte-for-byte copy only for alphanumeric-leading ids and otherwise the prefix+hex mapping so the image cannot equal another 4–40 run id.

findings.scenario: Every manifest field except packetDigest is unchanged; domains, implementationAuthorized=false, provider/deploy/release policy, and primaryPaths are untouched. packetDigest still moves f17059ec… → 7a34d7e5…. Architecture/threat-model paths are not domain packets in this manifest, and no supplied proof gives preimage, packet list, or SHA-256 command for 7a34d7e55c02034ac74a7db58fb1c25c7217f42501bbc7e72a0085482b925a67. The new digest is an unbound authority claim (drift if packets did not change; false binding if they did).
findings.remediation: Attach the canonical packet preimage and hash command that produce 7a34d7e55c02034ac74a7db58fb1c25c7217f42501bbc7e72a0085482b925a67, or revert packetDigest if the packet set is unchanged.

findings.scenario: The updated paragraph still opens “The Workbench exposes Agent Studio only in Edit mode” and then requires one current-run instance to remain mounted across View/Edit behind hidden+aria-hidden+inert. A reader applying the lead sentence unmounts on View and drops the process-only draft/receipt T3C1B retained.
findings.remediation: State interactive exposure as assistant∧Edit only; keep the mount/retention sentence as the normative current-run lifetime.

findings.scenario: “without an apply or automatic retry control” modifies only valid non-complete terminals. Complete results are merely “proposal-only”. The threat model also forbids apply/retry only on a terminal view, so the complete-proposal surface is not explicitly no-apply/no-auto-retry.
findings.remediation: State that both complete proposal and non-complete terminal views have no apply control and no automatic retry.

audit.proof_assessment: T3A–T3C2 are CLEAN static reviews (T3C2 is not a live run). They support read+propose-only deterministic no-provider placeholder, five-key envelope with exact complete binding and literal-null non-complete fail-closed, Local assignment receiving/sending no selection, keyed current-run Agent Studio retention with native hidden+aria-hidden+inert, internal inactive pane isolation, data-class as caller assertion, and Site advice remaining separate. They contradict architecture’s “path ID … echoed into the job”. The git slice supports packetDigest-only manifest editing with no widened domain/implementation/provider/deploy/release flags, but nothing verifies the new digest value.
residual_risks: Workbench collapse still unmounts Agent Studio (T3C1B unclaimed); architecture scopes retention to tool and View/Edit only.
“both process-local pane states” can be read as classifying mutating Site advice as process-only retention.
Data-class UI help copy is not quoted; threat-model examples (cookies, release, appointment) may not match the UI warning.
T3C2 live tab/0x0/network oracles were not attached; a11y claims rest on code review plus a static E2E script.
inert/hidden on the wrapper would not cover portal UI if Agent Studio ever portals (T3C1B residual).
